label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Dear all,

Just coming up for air after nights, and catching up with this properly.

First, Amma and Appa, I am genuinely thrilled you’re coming. Having you here for ordinary days, not just a hurried holiday, is something I’ve wanted for a long time. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”. Apparently your Tuesdays are spoken for, Amma.

Kiran, you’re right that I should have told you earlier. I started the paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and I should have looped you in then, rather than letting the first you heard be an announcement with things already under way. That’s on me. I’m sorry.

For a bit of background, the idea first came up on the phone in August, when Rohan was showing Appa the vegetable patch on video and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” We’ve talked about it since. That doesn’t change the fact that there was plenty of time for me to talk to you too.

On Appa’s heart, I agree we need a proper plan. Being a doctor myself isn’t a substitute for that, and we shouldn’t assume that treatment would be free on the NHS. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before they fly, and to do a video consultation in July. He’s also happy to share his notes with me, with Appa’s agreement, so we can have the relevant history and treatment details here.

I’ve got a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, about £640 each for the six months. The agent says Appa’s stent is covered, but I want to see that confirmed in the policy wording, including what emergency treatment and any exclusions actually look like, before we buy it. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from our house and I know half the cardiology team, which is reassuring practically, but it doesn’t remove the need for proper cover or Dr. Prakash’s advice about travelling.

The annexe at the back is finished now: ground floor, no steps, and their own shower with a grab rail. They’ll have their own space, rather than six months of living out of suitcases in our spare room.

Your point about Amma being away longer than she’s used to is fair too. Amma, this needn’t be a six-month commitment regardless of how you feel once you’re here. The return ticket will be flexible, and you can go home whenever you want. The visa is the UK long-term visitor visa, but it only allows a maximum of six months per visit. We’re planning the first week of April to the end of September 2027, with the exact dates kept within that limit.

And Pune needn’t be lost. One possibility is for Amma and Appa to fly from here to Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi in September and finish the trip there. Or you could all come here in August—I’d be very happy to cover the Pune family’s flights. We’d love to have everyone together. Neither needs deciding by email now.

Could we all have a video call this Sunday at 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? I’d like us to talk this through together, including what Amma and Appa want, rather than leave your concerns hanging or pretend everything is already settled.

Love,
Meera
